title: Smart Filter & Decision Tree for Privileged Admin Access Intake
creator: Asha Mirza
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and internal ops send a steady stream of non-bug admin/access requests (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM synchronization issues, org policy exceptions). Triage today is manual, inconsistent, and slow—leading to SLA misses, security risk spikes, and poor customer experience for customers on Dedicated/Private plans.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'Smart Filter' intake form and deterministic decision tree that automatically scores and routes privileged admin requests to the correct workflow (self-serve docs, automated-provisioning, Security review, Dedicated ops, Sales/AM liaison). The system must be auditable, extensible, and provide telemetry for tuning.

Scope: Intake UX + backend scoring service + routing rules + Console support portal integration + telemetry/dashboard for triage KPIs. Initially cover RBAC, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM sync, privileged API keys and org policy exception requests. Excludes full RBAC enforcement changes (handled in ENG execution tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form created in Console support portal with required fields: request type, affected org(s), requested roles/SCIM connector, SSO provider, justification, requested SLA, attachments.
Automated scoring module runs on submission and assigns a triage score (0-100) with visible rule breakdown in ticket metadata.
Decision tree routes >= 90% of incoming administrative requests to one of: self-serve guide, automated provisioning queue, security review queue, Dedicated ops queue, account team (Sales/AM).
False positive routing rate for Security queue under 10% in a 2-week sampling window (i.e., <10% benign tickets sent to Security).
Telemetry available in Console: daily intake volume by type, average time-to-first-assignment, queue backlog by route, and scoring distribution.
End-to-end tests cover form validation, scoring logic, routing, and webhook to ticketing system (Zendesk/ServiceNow mock).
Documentation and runbook published: how to adjust rule weights, add new request types, and audit decisions.
proposed_solution: 1) UX: Add a focused 'Admin & Access Request' flow in Console -> Support with conditional fields and SSO/RBAC templates. 2) Backend: Small scoring microservice that computes weighted score from signals: role sensitivity, number of affected users/org size, external provider involvement (SSO/SCIM), data access scope, SLA tier, and presence of attachments. 3) Decision tree: Deterministic rule set that maps score + request type to route; rules are editable via a small admin UI. 4) Integrations: Create a webhook that opens a ticket in support/ticketing with routing metadata and attaches audit log of decision. 5) Telemetry: Emit events for each stage and surface in a new 'Admin Intake' dashboard in Console. 6) Safety: Any high-scoring security-affecting requests must be flagged with 'security_review_required' and cannot be auto-approved.
implementation_steps: Design intake form fields and conditional flows (link to Figma mock).
Spec scoring signals and default weights with PM and Security input.
Ship scoring microservice MVP behind a feature flag; unit tests for each rule.
Create decision-tree engine mapping rules to target queues.
Add webhook integration to support ticketing (Zendesk dev sandbox) and mock ServiceNow for enterprise customers.
Build telemetry events and Dashboard prototype in Console (basic queries + charts).
Pilot with 2 enterprise customers and 3 internal support agents for 4 weeks and iterate weights.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: MVP behind feature flag in Console for internal agents and 2 pilot customers (2 weeks). Phase 2: Open to all enterprise customers with opt-in and monitoring (4 weeks). Phase 3: Full GA and replace ad-hoc email intake (release console-2026.04). Rollback plan: disable scoring feature flag and route all submissions to manual triage queue.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track: volume per request type, average triage latency (time to first assignment), routing accuracy (% correct queue after human review), security-queue false positive rate, pilot NPS of intake flow. Alert if average time-to-first-assignment > 24 hours or security-queue backlog > 10 tickets for >48h.
open_questions: What exact default weights should Security sign-off require (role sensitivity vs data exposure)?
Should SCIM mis-sync requests be auto-routed to infra or to customer support by default?
Do we need to include org-level policy exceptions or treat them as legal/compliance tickets?
Which ticketing systems do we prioritize for webhook reliability (Zendesk first, ServiceNow second)?
How should we surface the decision rationale to customers to avoid confusion?
decisions: Use deterministic decision tree (not ML) for MVP to keep auditability and explainability.
Expose per-ticket rule breakdown in support UI for faster human override and audit.
Flag any request that touches >1000 users or includes external identity providers as high-sensitivity automatically.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Security and Support — agreed on initial signal set and pilot customers.
2026-03-05: Figma intake mock v1 shared; design requests conditional SSO fields and attachments.
2026-03-10: ENG estimates scoring microservice at 5 points; dependency ENG-19872 logged for ticketing webhook.
2026-03-14: Security requested explicit audit log field and retention policy; added to acceptance criteria.
